content.value: A gate must red for exactly one reason - its own claim

Living wave Paper for the FOUNDING wave of `auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky` (priority 0). No charter exists yet; this wave's Decide phase writes D1+. Every later phase appends here - Digest adds the survey digest and verify plan, Decide adds the wave plan, Review closes it as the debrief.

STATUS: Strategize complete - the wave is SURVEYING. The direction below is COMMITTED but tentative in its details; two exploration rounds (survey, then verify) precede Decide, which finalises it. Nothing here is a proven claim unless it names the command that produced it.
MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard, carried from the wish): Fable 5 is spend-limited. Every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice - never 'fable'.
The wish, verbatim

THIS CYCLE: THE GATES TELL THE TRUTH. Every defect in this roster is a gate that lies - it reds when nothing is wrong, or it blocks work that is correct, and each one teaches readers to dismiss it. A dismissed gate is how a one-character CSS defect survived FIVE waves in production while three gates certified it green. Root task: auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky (priority 0).
What I read, and what it changed

The lead's roster is four proven defects. I read the actual surfaces before setting direction, because a direction set on an unread codebase is a guess - and this lead's briefs have been corrected twelve times today. Four things I found materially reframe the wave. Each is stated with the command that produced it, and each is handed to the verify fleet rather than assumed.
Finding 1 - the TOTP race is real, and the fix must not touch the server

`grep -rn 'NimbleTOTP.verification_code' api/test/` returns 25 call sites across 8 files (accounts_test.exs alone holds 11). The mechanism is confirmed by reading the call site: in `auth_controller_test.exs` `enroll_totp!/1`, the code is computed INLINE while building the request body, then an HTTP round-trip happens. If the 30-second period rolls in that gap, the server correctly rejects a stale code.

CRITICAL GUARDRAIL I want stated before any builder flies: `accounts.ex` `enable_totp/3` is a bare `NimbleTOTP.valid?(secret, code)` with NO drift tolerance, while `valid_totp?/2` and the verify path pass `totp_opts(user)` - which carries `since:`, the REPLAY guard (MEDIUM-6). Those two call sites differ for a reason. A builder who 'unifies' them, or who adds a drift window to make the test pass, converts a test flake into a SECURITY REGRESSION - a gate lying in the other direction, accepting what it should reject. The server is behaving correctly. The fix is entirely test-side.
Finding 2 - the OAuth flake has a named mechanism, and it is not the one filed

The lead's hypothesis was 'shared OAuth state mutated by a concurrent test'. Directionally right, wrong object. I chased and DISCARDED two candidates first: `OAuthStub` stores overrides in the PROCESS DICTIONARY (explicitly async-safe by design), and the `oauth_states` single-use nonce ledger is Repo-backed (sandboxed per async test). Neither can leak.

What can: `cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/oauth_test.exs` is `use BarkparkCloud.DataCase, async: true` and at its 'a provider with blank creds is excluded' test does `Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, patched)` where `patched` nulls github's `client_secret`, asserts `enabled_providers() == ["google"]`, and restores on_exit. `Application.put_env/3` writes ONE value for the WHOLE NODE. While that test holds the swap, github is DISABLED process-wide - and `router_oauth_test.exs`, a different `async: true` module, is calling `/v1/auth/oauth/github/callback`. A disabled provider yields exactly the observed symptom: the FIRST redemption returning `/#oauth_error=oauth_failed` where `#oauth=` was asserted. Seed-dependent, because it is a race.
Finding 3 - the repo already has a tripwire for this exact class, scoped to one key

`cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` exists. It was built for this flake class after `sites_deploy_test.exs` swapped `:site_box_relay` globally and red `router_sites_test.exs`. Its `@shared_seam_keys` list contains exactly ONE entry: `:site_box_relay`. Its own moduledoc closes with a prediction:

Other config keys are swapped by async modules too, but each of those is read by only its own module today; if that ever changes, add the key to @shared_seam_keys rather than re-learning this the hard way.

We are re-learning it the hard way. The `OAuth` config key IS now read by a second async module. The guard's stated precondition is false, and the guard did not notice because the list is hand-maintained. This is the single most important artifact in the wave - it is proof that the fix shape proposed below WORKS, and proof of exactly how it decays when scoped to the one instance that bit us.
Finding 4 - the format gate is not red-by-accident, it is red BY DESIGN

The lead filed this as 'red on main across 91 files'. The file tells a different and worse story. `.github/workflows/elixir.yml` sets the format job `continue-on-error: true`, names it 'Format (mix format --check-formatted, advisory)', and documents WHY: prod pins Elixir 1.18.1, local dev runs 1.19.x, their formatters disagree, and running `mix format` locally is FORBIDDEN by CLAUDE.md. The comment ends: 'until then this job stays visible as a drift signal, not a blocker.'

So this is not a gate that broke. This is a gate that was DECLAWED instead of fixed, and left on screen. It is structurally incapable of being green, it reds every PR including docs-only ones, and it blocks nothing. That is the terminal stage of the disease the wish names - and it is the same story as the one-character CSS defect that survived five waves: a signal nobody could act on, so nobody read it.
The pattern under all four
Each defect is a CORRECT INSIGHT APPLIED AT SAMPLE SCOPE INSTEAD OF POPULATION SCOPE. Nobody here was wrong. Everybody stopped at the instance that bit them.

TOTP - the race is understood; 1 of 25 call sites was going to be fixed. OAuth - the async-global-seam class is understood AND tripwired; the tripwire lists 1 of N keys. pr-task-gate - the invariant is understood ('this change is task-backed'); the predicate encodes one sample of it ('someone is actively typing right now'). format - the toolchain drift is understood; the response was to declaw the signal rather than fix the population of 91 files.

Restated as the law this wave proposes: A GATE MUST BE ABLE TO BE GREEN, ABLE TO BE RED, AND MUST RED FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON - the thing it claims to measure. Every defect here is a predicate contaminated by a variable with nothing to do with its claim: wall clock, scheduler seed, worker liveness, toolchain version. `continue-on-error` is not a third option; it is how a contaminated gate becomes permanent furniture.
DIRECTION - fix populations, and make the hazard unwritable
This wave does NOT fix four failing things. It closes four populations, and leaves each one unable to reopen. Every slice lands in three parts, and a slice missing part three is not done:

(1) THE CAUSE - remove the contaminating variable, never retry around it. (2) THE POPULATION - migrate every sibling instance, not the sample that failed. (3) THE RATCHET - a tripwire that fails CI if the hazardous shape reappears, plus an affordance that makes the safe path the easy one. A fix without a ratchet is a fix with a half-life.

Part three is the boldest and most durable move, and it is not speculative: `async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` is that exact shape, already in the tree, already having caught its class once. The wave's job is to finish what was left at sample scope - and to make the seam list DERIVED rather than hand-maintained, so it cannot silently go stale again.
The slices I lean toward (Decide finalises)

S1 - TOTP, the population of 25. Build a shared window-stable helper: compute the seconds remaining in the current period and, if the headroom is below a threshold, wait out the boundary BEFORE generating, so generation and server validation are guaranteed to land in the same period. Then migrate all 25 sites. Then a tripwire: raw `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` in `api/test/` fails CI. Server code is NOT touched - that is a fence, not a preference.

S2 - OAuth, the seam class. Fix `oauth_test.exs` by isolation-by-construction (the guard's own prescribed remedy: test the predicate by naming/passing config directly rather than globally swapping), OR mark that module `async: false` if the read surface genuinely requires the global. Then GENERALISE the guard: derive the shared-key set instead of hand-listing it, so any config key read by two or more async modules is protected automatically.

S3 - pr-task-gate, the invariant. Re-specify the predicate around what the gate actually means - 'this change is task-backed' - not 'someone is actively typing'. A task closed on met acceptance criteria is the SUCCESS case, not a violation; a well-authored task whose criteria are 'committed / mutation-proven / live run returns X' is legitimately closed before its PR merges, and that deadlocked three PRs today. Two mechanical sub-defects ride along: the workflow has no `types:` filter so it inherits [opened, synchronize, reopened] - adding `edited` lets a corrected PR body re-fire and dissolves the sticky-404. Note the 404 path must STAY definitive: it correctly caught an invented task id today. `scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh` already exists and is the mutation-proof vehicle.

S4 - format. This is a DECIDE-TIME CALL, and it should be argued rather than defaulted. The honest options are (a) fix the 91 files in a session pinned to prod Elixir 1.18.1, or (b) DELETE the job. What is NOT an option is leaving a permanently-red advisory check on screen. The lean is (b)-or-defer: formatting 91 files WILL conflict with two live cycles holding `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` and `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*`, and a deferral stated out loud with its reason is itself a truth-telling act. Silently leaving it is the only losing move.
Direction debate - the rivals, and why this won

RIVAL A - 'Fix the four.' Straight roster execution: four slices, four fixes, four mutation proofs. Bounded, safe, obviously in scope. It loses on the wish's own terms: the wish is not 'these four checks are broken', it is 'gates teach readers to dismiss them'. Four patches with no ratchet leaves the generating process untouched, and the tree already shows what that costs - the seam guard is a wave-old fix whose class immediately regrew in an unlisted key. Rival A would have fixed 1 of 25 TOTP sites and called it done.

RIVAL B - 'Flake observability first.' Build a harness (seed-randomised N-run loop, per-test failure history, a quarantine ledger) before fixing anything, on the theory that you cannot trust gates you cannot measure. Genuinely tempting and it foreclosed the least. It loses on sequencing: the roster is ALREADY proven by hand, by re-run, with the prediction registered before the re-run. Instrumentation would spend the wave and land zero honest gates. Partially absorbed instead: method law already demands 20-30 seed-randomised runs per fix, so that loop gets written as a reusable script rather than a bespoke epic.

RIVAL C - 'Charter first.' This is a founding wave with no charter; make the law the deliverable and the four fixes its proof cases. It loses as a PRIMARY framing - a charter written before the four fixes are attempted would be legislating from theory, and this lead's theory has been corrected twelve times today. Absorbed as a BYPRODUCT: Decide writes D1+ from what the builders actually learn, which is the right order.

WHY THE WINNER WON: it is the only candidate whose success condition is 'the defect class cannot recur', which is the only thing that stops teaching dismissal. And crucially it is not a theory - the repo contains a working instance of the exact shape (the seam guard) AND a working instance of its decay (that guard's one-key list). The evidence for the direction was already in the tree.
The sharpest attack on the winner

SCOPE EXPLOSION. Four gates, a 25-site migration, a derived-seam-key generaliser, a re-specified merge gate with hermetic tests, plus 91 files of formatting - against a hard surface fence and two live cycles in `api/`. This is the attack to take most seriously, and it is how the wave absorbs it:

- The 25-site TOTP migration is MECHANICAL once the helper exists, and `api/test/` is inside our fence, so it collides with nobody. It is one slice, not twenty-five. - The format gate defaults to DEFER-WITH-A-STATED-REASON precisely to remove the 91-file conflict; the wave is allowed to not do it, but not allowed to be quiet about it. - The 'sweep for other contaminated predicates' is SURVEY AND VERIFY work, not build work. It produces filed tasks for wave 2, not slices in wave 1. Width is cheap in the fleets and expensive in the builders.

SECOND ATTACK: the OAuth mechanism is a strategist's reading, not a proof. If the `put_env` collision is not the cause, S2 has no fix. Absorbed by aiming a verifier at exactly one job - reproduce it deterministically (force the interleave, seed 792404, `async: true` audit of `cloud/test/`) BEFORE any builder flies. If reproduction fails, S2 becomes 'instrument and quarantine with a stated reason', which is still honest, and still not a retry wrapper.

THIRD ATTACK: a builder takes the cheap road on S1 and adds drift tolerance to `accounts.ex`, turning a test flake into an auth weakening. Absorbed by making 'server code is not touched' an explicit slice fence, and by pointing the verify fleet at the `totp_opts`/`since:` replay-guard asymmetry before Decide writes the brief.
Method law for this wave (non-negotiable)
A RETRY WRAPPER IS NOT A FIX. It hides the race and preserves the lie. Any slice whose proof is 'it passed this time' is rejected at Review.

EVERY FIX MUST BE PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL. Force the failure condition; show the OLD path breaks there and the NEW one does not. For TOTP that means forcing a window boundary. For OAuth it means forcing the config interleave. Then run the target suite 20-30 times with randomised seeds - not once.

RUN WHERE DEPS RESOLVE. A fresh worktree without `mix deps.get` fails with 'Unknown dependency :ecto_sql given to :import_deps', and at the exit-code level that error is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real failure. A mutation test run there measures the dep error, not the thing. The lead hit this today.

SURFACE FENCE. This cycle owns `api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/`, `cloud/test/`, `.github/workflows/pr-task-gate.yml`, `scripts/pr-task-gate.sh`. S1's population extends the api/test fence to the 8 files holding the 25 call sites. DO NOT touch `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` (Studio wave 11 RUNNING), `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*` (PDS wave 10 RUNNING), `tooling/grip/`, or `api/lib/barkpark/content|portable_doc`.
Survey plan - what the fleet is being sent to find, and why

Fifteen broad assignments, one Sonnet each. Width is cheap here and buys precise depth later. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question, including the ones already believed answered - a strategist's reading is a hypothesis, not a finding.

s1-totp-population - Enumerate all 25 `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` call sites in api/test/ and classify each by the GAP between generation and validation: same-process direct function call, HTTP round-trip, or multi-step. Which are actually boundary-crossable?  WHY: Decides whether one helper covers all 25 or the population splits into two shapes needing different remedies.

s2-totp-server-asymmetry - Map every NimbleTOTP.valid? call site in api/lib/. Why does enable_totp/3 pass no opts while valid_totp?/2 and the verify path pass totp_opts(user)? What does `since:` actually guard, and what breaks if they are unified?  WHY: The number-one way a builder turns this test fix into a security regression. Must be fenced explicitly in the brief.

s3-oauth-interleave - Confirm or refute: does oauth_test.exs's Application.put_env of the OAuth key (nulling github client_secret) disable github process-wide while router_oauth_test.exs concurrently calls the github callback? Trace how a disabled provider surfaces - is /#oauth_error=oauth_failed the exact symptom?  WHY: This is the central OAuth claim and S2's entire basis. If false, S2 needs a different mechanism.

s4-seam-guard-anatomy - Read async_global_seam_guard_test.exs fully. How does it detect offenders, why is @shared_seam_keys hand-maintained, and what would a DERIVED version need - can 'config keys read by 2+ async modules' be computed statically from the test tree?  WHY: Determines whether the ratchet for S2 is a one-line list addition or a real generaliser. Feasibility gates ambition.

s5-async-putenv-census - Census every Application.put_env in cloud/test/ AND api/test/: which module, is it async:true, which config key, is it restored on_exit, and is that key read by any other async module?  WHY: Sizes the true population behind S2. The seam guard's own moduledoc predicts this list has grown; measure it.

Enumerate every state a legitimately-worked task can be in when its PR opens.  WHY: S3 rewrites the predicate; it must be rewritten against the real intent, and the doc may already state it correctly.

s7-gate-trigger-mechanics - Confirm pr-task-gate.yml has no `types:` filter (inheriting opened/synchronize/reopened), and establish whether adding `edited` re-fires on a PR body edit. Also check the merge-base grandfather clause and the hotfix! lane for interactions.  WHY: The cheapest high-value fix in the wave, and the grandfather/hotfix paths must not be broken by it.

s8-format-gate-truth - Verify the format gate's real state: is it continue-on-error, is it red on main right now, and is the count 91 files (25 lib/, 66 test/)? Is the Elixir 1.18.1-vs-1.19.x formatter-divergence rationale still accurate?  WHY: The lead's item 4 was already corrected once from a truncated read. S4's decision needs the real number and the real cause.

s9-format-conflict-map - If the 91 files were formatted, which overlap the two live cycles (api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/, api/tenancy, scripts/pds-*)? Is there a conflict-free subset, and how large?  WHY: Decides whether S4 can be scoped safely or must be deferred outright. Determines fix-vs-delete-vs-defer.

s10-prior-art - bp search papers and tasks for prior work on flaky tests, gate honesty, async seam races, merge gates, and de-flaking - including the sites_deploy/router_sites incident that produced the seam guard, and charter GR47.  WHY: This wave must not re-solve what a prior wave already ruled on; GR47 is referenced by the guard and has not been read.

s11-other-lying-gates - Audit every workflow in .github/workflows/ for the same disease: continue-on-error jobs, checks red on main today, checks that fire on irrelevant paths, and required-vs-advisory status. Which are structurally unable to be green?  WHY: The population question applied to the gates themselves. Likely the richest source of wave-2 tasks.

s12-flake-history - Sample recent CI history on main and PRs: which tests have failed and then passed on re-run of an identical commit? Rank by frequency.  WHY: Tests whether the four filed defects are the top of the population or just the ones the lead happened to see.

WHY: Generalises S2 beyond config: put_env is one global seam and probably not the only one.

WHY: Method law depends on builders not measuring a dep error. This must be written into every brief verbatim.

s15-seed-repro-tooling - What tooling exists for repeated seed-randomised runs (mix test --seed, --repeat-until-failure, ExUnit config, any existing scripts)? What is the cheapest reliable 20-30x loop for the auth suite and cloud OAuth suite?  WHY: Every slice's proof depends on this loop. If it does not exist it must be built once and shared, not per-slice.

DIGEST — 15 survey reports folded in; the verify fleet is flying

STATUS: Survey complete. The wave is VERIFYING. 15 surveyors returned; this section states what they established, where they CONTRADICT each other or my direction, what nobody checked, and the 12 verify assignments now in flight. Decide follows the verify round and finalises the slice plan.
What the survey ESTABLISHED

S1 TOTP — settled, and sharper than filed. 25 call sites across 8 files, reproduced independently by three surveyors (grep -rn NimbleTOTP.verification_code api/test/ | wc -l = 25; -rl | wc -l = 8). They split into two shapes, and the split matters for RISK, not for the remedy: 16 are same-process direct calls into Accounts.enable_totp/valid_totp?/verify_totp with zero intervening I/O (microsecond gap, no failure of this shape ever observed), and 9 are HTTP round-trips through Phoenix.ConnTest post() where the gap is tens-to-hundreds of ms. BOTH confirmed real-world failures (auth_controller_test.exs:31 via enroll_totp!/1 driving the :427 failure that red main, and the PR #4920 sighting near :191) are the HTTP shape. One window-stable helper covers both shapes; the migration is uniform mechanical substitution at all 25 sites.

The HARD FENCE is now better-argued than when I wrote it. accounts.ex:598 enable_totp/3 is a bare NimbleTOTP.valid?(secret, code); :632 valid_totp?/2 and :652 verify_totp/2 both pass totp_opts(user) = [since: last_totp_at] (:686). The `since:` guard is NimbleTOTP's reused?/3 (api/deps/nimble_totp/lib/nimble_totp.ex:249-256): it rejects any code whose period floor-divides to <= the since timestamp's period, regardless of digit correctness — the RFC 6238 one-time-use guarantee. enable_totp OMITS it correctly: disable_totp/1 (accounts.ex:617-622) does NOT clear last_totp_at (only reset_mfa:true password reset does, :541-553), so a disable-then-re-enable cycle carries a stale timestamp from the OLD secret into the NEW secret's enrolment — passing totp_opts there would spuriously REJECT a perfectly valid brand-new code. And the trap is baked into the dependency: NimbleTOTP's own moduledoc (deps/nimble_totp/lib/nimble_totp.ex:218-232) PRESCRIBES the grace-window pattern (call valid? at time and at time - period) that a builder chasing this flake would reach for. Doing that on valid_totp?/verify_totp triples the live acceptance window from 30s to ~90s on two internet-facing endpoints (session_controller.ex:372, auth_controller.ex:122) and widens the replay surface MEDIUM-6 exists to close. grep for period:/grace/drift in accounts.ex returns NOTHING today — the fence protects a currently-clean invariant.

S2 OAuth — my strategist's reading was RIGHT, and it is already filed with a reproduction. Four surveyors independently confirmed the mechanism by direct code read: cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/oauth_test.exs:8 is `use DataCase, async: true` and its blank-creds test (:33-44) does Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, patched) at :39, nulling github's client_secret for the whole test body (on_exit restore at :40) — a whole-node write. cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/oauth.ex:329 reads `defp config, do: Application.get_env(...)` FRESH on every call, no caching. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_oauth_test.exs:7 is ALSO async:true and drives GET /v1/auth/oauth/github/callback in ~10 tests. router.ex:898-920 fails at the FIRST `with` clause (OAuth.enabled?) and redirects to /#oauth_error=oauth_failed — never a 404 — which is EXACTLY the asserted-vs-observed mismatch. A third independent CI sighting: run 29744055238 job 88357533276, RouterOAuthTest replay-state test failed then passed on rerun of the identical commit.

CRITICAL for Decide: this is ALREADY a filed, root-caused, reproduced, fix-speced OPEN task — `cloud-oauth-replay-test-is-seed-flaky` (priority 1, 0/7 acceptance criteria, unclaimed). It contains a live reproduction (a probe racing a 50ms blank-creds window deterministically observed {:error, :provider_not_enabled}), proof the seam guard is VACUOUSLY GREEN today, proof that adding the module-form key "OAuth" to @shared_seam_keys flips the guard RED and correctly names oauth_test.exs, and a fix under charter D28 (extract the blank-creds test to an async:false oauth_blank_creds_test.exs + add the key) that explicitly REJECTS retry wrappers and config-injection refactors. It is parented to a DIFFERENT wave paper (production-truth-wave-2026-07-20) and risks sitting orphaned across two waves. Decide ADOPTS and re-parents it. It does NOT re-file it.

The ratchet decay is worse than I diagnosed — it happened TWICE, in two directories, independently. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs is a 63-line pure source-TEXT scanner: Path.wildcard("test/**/*_test.exs") relative to cloud/, keep files containing the literal "async: true", then String.contains? on "Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, #{key}" for each key in a HAND-MAINTAINED @shared_seam_keys (:36) holding exactly [":site_box_relay"]. It only inspects WRITES; it never looks at reads; it cannot discover a new shared key; and it structurally cannot see api/test at all. Meanwhile api/test/barkpark/application_env_isolation_test.exs is the residue of an EARLIER, INDEPENDENT sample-scope fix of the identical class (task-435b89bfa992a58a flipped MediaTest, StudioChatTest and Plugins.GithubTest from async:true to async:false) — and it is a single demonstration test, not a scanner. Two teams, two directories, the same hazard, two correct-but-sample-scoped fixes, neither aware of the other, neither of which swept its own tree. That is the wave's thesis proven twice, not asserted once.

The hazard population is now BOUNDED and countable, which is a real narrowing. Application env is the ONLY live global-state channel: ETS, :persistent_term, named GenServers, and shared-path filesystem writes were all checked across both trees' async:true modules and are CLEAN (the one :ets hit, supervision_isolation_test.exs:104, creates an UNNAMED table; the ~40 Registry.register hits are the app's own BarkparkCloud.Registry domain model, not OTP process registry — a discarded false positive). So the guard needs SCOPE generalisation (which keys, which directory), not new state categories. Population: 7 async:true node-global swappers in cloud/test — oauth_test.exs, github_test.exs, billing_reconcile_isolation_test.exs, cloudflare_test.exs, vercel_test.exs, web/router_test.exs (:platform_admin_emails), web/usage_route_test.exs — a list three surveyors reproduced independently and which matches the already-filed audit task-04054d483ae95bd1 EXACTLY. Plus 2 previously UNFILED in api/test: media/image_backend/vix_test.exs:2,151 and search/intelligence_test.exs:2,242 (the latter's key :search_intel_record_async is read at api/lib/barkpark/search/intelligence.ex:567). Both are latent-not-live today — which is precisely the state :site_box_relay was in before it bit gr-p5-cloud-flake.

S3 pr-task-gate — settled, with no doc/code disagreement to fix. merge-gates.md §7, the workflow header comment, and the founding task tob-w1-ci-task-gate all describe the SAME narrow predicate the script implements: task exists AND lifecycle_status == in_progress AND claim.worker present. The current predicate IS the original design, not drift from it. The gap is predicate-versus-invariant: of the 9 lifecycle states a legitimately-worked task can occupy when its PR opens, exactly ONE passes. `done` — the state the task discipline REQUIRES when criteria are 'committed / mutation-proven / live run returns X' and none of them is 'PR merged' — is rejected as if no work happened. Mechanically confirmed: pr-task-gate.yml:30-33 is a bare `pull_request:` with no `types:` key, inheriting opened/synchronize/reopened. CORRECTION (2026-07-20, Review): the S2 population was 9, not 10

The Decide section above ("S2 - THE POPULATION IS 10, NOT 7") states that cloud/test holds 8 async:true Application env swappers, counting registry/cloudflare_credential_test.exs as the one the filed audit missed. The build refuted that. That file's ONLY occurrence of Application.put_env is moduledoc prose at line 12, saying the token is threaded as an argument and "never smuggled through Application.put_env". It is not a swapper and was correctly left alone.

The true population is 9: seven in cloud/test (oauth, github, billing_reconcile_isolation, vercel, cloudflare, web/router, web/usage_route) and two in api/test (media/image_backend/vix, search/intelligence). The Decide-time census was itself a naive text scan that over-matched on prose - this wave's own thesis applied to this wave's own paperwork, caught by the builder and stamped as a deviation. Left as a dated correction rather than a silent rewrite, per the charter's own standard.
DEBRIEF - what the founding wave actually shipped

All five slices built, reviewed, and green. They five-way merge onto origin/main with no conflicts; on the integrated tree the cloud suite is 2150/0, the api gate suites are 0 failures, and all four new ratchets are green together. GRADE: A.
Per slice, as it will merge

S1 hg-w1-totp-window-stable-population -> loop-epic/totp-window-stable-helper-across-all-25--0-r. All 25 raw generator sites migrated, 0 remaining outside the helper; the helper is a targeted boundary wait proven a no-op on 93.3% of the period by an exhaustive 30,000-offset sweep, not a blanket sleep. Gate on final state: 137 tests / 0 failures at --max-cases 8, format clean, api/lib untouched. The reviewer independently re-proved FENCE B by applying the CAREFUL grace-window mutation (since: threaded through both valid? calls): it reds accounts_test.exs:432 and NOTHING ELSE - a precise detector with zero collateral.

S2 hg-w1-async-seam-ban-and-scanner -> loop-epic/ban-application-put-env-inside-async-tru-1-r. Nine swappers isolated with a per-file comment naming the exact key and, where known, the observed race. @shared_seam_keys deleted; the predicate is now the one question source text can answer, run over BOTH roots from absolute paths, with a reason-required escape hatch and anti-vacuity assertions. cloud 2150/0; cloud/lib unchanged.

S3 hg-w1-pr-task-gate-task-backed -> loop-epic/pr-task-gate-close-the-fixture-hole-firs-2-r. The fixtures-first order was respected and PROVEN: the two new fixtures are the only ones that catch deletion of the lifecycle check, which left the old 9-fixture set fully green. Predicate is now task-backed, not who-is-typing; 404 stays definitive; edited added. 9 -> 20 fixtures, shellcheck clean.

S4 hg-w1-format-drift-ceiling -> loop-epic/migrate-the-50-conflict-free-api-format--3-r. Drift 92 -> 42, population regenerated by measurement rather than pasted, and a shrink-only ceiling installed as its own BLOCKING job - deliberately separate, because continue-on-error is a JOB-level setting and putting the ratchet inside the Format job would have made it unable to fail.

S5 hg-w1-never-cancel-main-population -> loop-epic/cancelled-is-a-non-pass-give-cloud-yml-a-4-r. cloud.yml and doc-gates.yml both carry the ref guard; the population grep across all seven concurrency-bearing workflows returns 0 bare trues, and the whole-tree cross-tab found architecture.yml correctly benign (pull_request-only). Ratchet + bundled selftest, live-mutation proven.
What the review fixed in place

Five defects, and the striking thing is that every one is this epic's own disease living inside a gate built to cure it. That is not an indictment of the builders - it is evidence the standard is genuinely hard to meet, and it is why this wave needed a reviewer rather than a rubber stamp.

1. S5's ratchet went SILENT exactly when it could not run. Under set -e the assignment RESULT="$(scan ...)" aborts the script when scan exits 2, so a missing PyYAML produced exit 2 with a COMPLETELY EMPTY log - stdout and stderr both verified empty before the fix. The script cites charter D3 (only stdout text can discriminate a dep error from a real verdict) and then discarded that text. Both call sites now capture the status and re-emit.

2. S5's predicate UNDER-detected. It read only a literal branches: [main] list, so three valid shapes that DO fire on main were classed PR-only and their bare true passed as a harmless NOTE: push: with no branches filter at all, a glob or scalar (ma*n), and branches-ignore that does not name main. Now fnmatch-resolved with branches-ignore inverted; four new fixtures, and branches-ignore: [main] stays correctly safe.

3. S1's ratchet could pass VACUOUSLY. A wrong @test_root makes Path.wildcard return [], the offender list is trivially empty, and the gate passes having measured nothing. S2's sibling guard in this same wave defends exactly this; S1's did not - the two ratchets held different standards for their own honesty. Now asserts >100 files scanned and that the allowlisted helper is among them; proven able to fail.

4. S2's predicate missed formatter-WRAPPED use declarations and put_all_env. mix format splits a long "use ...Case, async: true" across two lines, and the per-line async match saw neither half - a module could carry a node-global put_env straight through the ratchet. Both closed, pinned by four fixtures including a wrapped async: FALSE case so the continuation-joining cannot become an over-matcher.

5. S3 read its parser output WHITESPACE-split. Nothing constrains a ledger claim.worker to a slug, and a value containing a space shifted every later field one position - the gate then returned a confident verdict computed from the wrong values. Worst case was a FALSE PASS: EXPECTED_WORKER=fable matching a task claimed by 'fable tob'. Now tab-separated, with tabs and newlines squashed at the emitter so the separator cannot be forged from the data side.
Two things the lead must know before merging

S4's toolchain skew is smaller than filed but still OPEN. The format-ceiling job is BLOCKING with no paths filter, and the roster was generated on local Elixir 1.19.5 against CI's pinned 1.18.1. New measurement this review: the entire cloud/ tree is format-clean under local 1.19.5, and cloud.yml runs the identical check BLOCKING and GREEN on the pin - a project's worth of Elixir on which the two formatters agree byte-for-byte. That does NOT cover the 50 migrated files' specific constructs. Read the PR's own format-ceiling job output. If it reds on files nobody touched, REGENERATE .format-drift-ceiling on the pin; never add continue-on-error to the ceiling job.

S1 x S4 interaction: settled by running it, not by arguing. S1's builder warned the two slices could disagree by up to 8 files if S4 committed a baseline computed before S1 merged. A real merge of the two branches shows the ceiling PASSES at 39 against its ceiling of 42 and names exactly the three roster files S1 formatted, with the lower-the-baseline notice. Shrink-only does the right thing. After both merge, lower count: to 39 and drop those three lines.

Merge-gated criteria the LEAD closes, one per slice: S1 criterion 9, S2 criterion 8, S3 criterion 7, S4 criterion 8, S5 criterion 4 - all worded "PR merged to main". S5 criterion 2 is additionally unproven at builder scope (it requires the PR's own cloud.yml and doc-gates.yml checks to CONCLUDE with quoted names and conclusions) and is honestly stamped --miss, as is S4's criterion 1 attempt note on toolchain skew. Neither is a stall; both need a real CI run.
Ledger audit

Clean. All five slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with claims held, evidence stamped as the work happened rather than batched, and merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - exactly the contract. Both honest --miss notes (S4 criterion 1, S5 criterion 2) are present with substantive text rather than a bare flag. Every honest-gates task updated today is a child of the epic; nothing outside the wave was touched. Twelve backlog children are filed, published and open.

One ledger addition by the reviewer: hg-bl-pr-task-gate-expected-worker-actor-drift (p3). The S3 builder identified this trap and wrote "I did not file this, and probably should have" - EXPECTED_WORKER now compares against closed_by for done tasks, which is zero-impact today because .github/pr-task-workers.json does not exist, but becomes a false red on a builder-authored PR against a lead-closed task the day anyone adds that map.
What the next wave should take

Branch protection (wave-2 item 1), first and above the rest of the roster. Charter D13 is the load-bearing gap: nothing in this repo is required-by-name, so every ratchet this wave built - all four of them, plus the ones already here - is advisory. This wave made the gates honest; protection is what makes honesty consequential. The path-filter skip-shim is its mandatory first step, because only 2 of 34 workflows run unconditionally on every PR and a required paths-filtered check sits Pending forever and deadlocks the repo. Tier 1 is TWO checks on day one, not eight.

Then, in order: the Quiz.Bridge sandbox cascade (a third distinct hazard shape neither existing fix covers, and it masked 1310 failures in one run); the :barkpark_rate_limiter whole-node ETS seam (which S1's builder hit directly - it is why --repeat-until-failure dies at repetition 3 with HTTP 429); Sobelow's red-under-green; then format completion and promotion once PRs #5016/#5015/#5014 release the Studio bucket. hg-bl-totp-ratchet-cloud-test-root deserves a note: cloud/test has 16 raw TOTP generator sites the api-scoped ratchet structurally cannot see - the exact mirror of charter D6, rediscovered independently one more time.

body.html:
A gate must red for exactly one reason - its own claim

Living wave Paper for the FOUNDING wave of `auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky` (priority 0). No charter exists yet; this wave's Decide phase writes D1+. Every later phase appends here - Digest adds the survey digest and verify plan, Decide adds the wave plan, Review closes it as the debrief.

STATUS: Strategize complete - the wave is SURVEYING. The direction below is COMMITTED but tentative in its details; two exploration rounds (survey, then verify) precede Decide, which finalises it. Nothing here is a proven claim unless it names the command that produced it.

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard, carried from the wish): Fable 5 is spend-limited. Every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice - never 'fable'.

The wish, verbatim

THIS CYCLE: THE GATES TELL THE TRUTH. Every defect in this roster is a gate that lies - it reds when nothing is wrong, or it blocks work that is correct, and each one teaches readers to dismiss it. A dismissed gate is how a one-character CSS defect survived FIVE waves in production while three gates certified it green. Root task: auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky (priority 0).

What I read, and what it changed

The lead's roster is four proven defects. I read the actual surfaces before setting direction, because a direction set on an unread codebase is a guess - and this lead's briefs have been corrected twelve times today. Four things I found materially reframe the wave. Each is stated with the command that produced it, and each is handed to the verify fleet rather than assumed.

Finding 1 - the TOTP race is real, and the fix must not touch the server

`grep -rn 'NimbleTOTP.verification_code' api/test/` returns 25 call sites across 8 files (accounts_test.exs alone holds 11). The mechanism is confirmed by reading the call site: in `auth_controller_test.exs` `enroll_totp!/1`, the code is computed INLINE while building the request body, then an HTTP round-trip happens. If the 30-second period rolls in that gap, the server correctly rejects a stale code.

CRITICAL GUARDRAIL I want stated before any builder flies: `accounts.ex` `enable_totp/3` is a bare `NimbleTOTP.valid?(secret, code)` with NO drift tolerance, while `valid_totp?/2` and the verify path pass `totp_opts(user)` - which carries `since:`, the REPLAY guard (MEDIUM-6). Those two call sites differ for a reason. A builder who 'unifies' them, or who adds a drift window to make the test pass, converts a test flake into a SECURITY REGRESSION - a gate lying in the other direction, accepting what it should reject. The server is behaving correctly. The fix is entirely test-side.

Finding 2 - the OAuth flake has a named mechanism, and it is not the one filed

The lead's hypothesis was 'shared OAuth state mutated by a concurrent test'. Directionally right, wrong object. I chased and DISCARDED two candidates first: `OAuthStub` stores overrides in the PROCESS DICTIONARY (explicitly async-safe by design), and the `oauth_states` single-use nonce ledger is Repo-backed (sandboxed per async test). Neither can leak.

What can: `cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/oauth_test.exs` is `use BarkparkCloud.DataCase, async: true` and at its 'a provider with blank creds is excluded' test does `Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, patched)` where `patched` nulls github's `client_secret`, asserts `enabled_providers() == ["google"]`, and restores on_exit. `Application.put_env/3` writes ONE value for the WHOLE NODE. While that test holds the swap, github is DISABLED process-wide - and `router_oauth_test.exs`, a different `async: true` module, is calling `/v1/auth/oauth/github/callback`. A disabled provider yields exactly the observed symptom: the FIRST redemption returning `/#oauth_error=oauth_failed` where `#oauth=` was asserted. Seed-dependent, because it is a race.

Finding 3 - the repo already has a tripwire for this exact class, scoped to one key

`cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` exists. It was built for this flake class after `sites_deploy_test.exs` swapped `:site_box_relay` globally and red `router_sites_test.exs`. Its `@shared_seam_keys` list contains exactly ONE entry: `:site_box_relay`. Its own moduledoc closes with a prediction:

Other config keys are swapped by async modules too, but each of those is read by only its own module today; if that ever changes, add the key to @shared_seam_keys rather than re-learning this the hard way.

We are re-learning it the hard way. The `OAuth` config key IS now read by a second async module. The guard's stated precondition is false, and the guard did not notice because the list is hand-maintained. This is the single most important artifact in the wave - it is proof that the fix shape proposed below WORKS, and proof of exactly how it decays when scoped to the one instance that bit us.

Finding 4 - the format gate is not red-by-accident, it is red BY DESIGN

The lead filed this as 'red on main across 91 files'. The file tells a different and worse story. `.github/workflows/elixir.yml` sets the format job `continue-on-error: true`, names it 'Format (mix format --check-formatted, advisory)', and documents WHY: prod pins Elixir 1.18.1, local dev runs 1.19.x, their formatters disagree, and running `mix format` locally is FORBIDDEN by CLAUDE.md. The comment ends: 'until then this job stays visible as a drift signal, not a blocker.'

So this is not a gate that broke. This is a gate that was DECLAWED instead of fixed, and left on screen. It is structurally incapable of being green, it reds every PR including docs-only ones, and it blocks nothing. That is the terminal stage of the disease the wish names - and it is the same story as the one-character CSS defect that survived five waves: a signal nobody could act on, so nobody read it.

The pattern under all four

Each defect is a CORRECT INSIGHT APPLIED AT SAMPLE SCOPE INSTEAD OF POPULATION SCOPE. Nobody here was wrong. Everybody stopped at the instance that bit them.

TOTP - the race is understood; 1 of 25 call sites was going to be fixed. OAuth - the async-global-seam class is understood AND tripwired; the tripwire lists 1 of N keys. pr-task-gate - the invariant is understood ('this change is task-backed'); the predicate encodes one sample of it ('someone is actively typing right now'). format - the toolchain drift is understood; the response was to declaw the signal rather than fix the population of 91 files.

Restated as the law this wave proposes: A GATE MUST BE ABLE TO BE GREEN, ABLE TO BE RED, AND MUST RED FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON - the thing it claims to measure. Every defect here is a predicate contaminated by a variable with nothing to do with its claim: wall clock, scheduler seed, worker liveness, toolchain version. `continue-on-error` is not a third option; it is how a contaminated gate becomes permanent furniture.

DIRECTION - fix populations, and make the hazard unwritable

This wave does NOT fix four failing things. It closes four populations, and leaves each one unable to reopen. Every slice lands in three parts, and a slice missing part three is not done:

(1) THE CAUSE - remove the contaminating variable, never retry around it. (2) THE POPULATION - migrate every sibling instance, not the sample that failed. (3) THE RATCHET - a tripwire that fails CI if the hazardous shape reappears, plus an affordance that makes the safe path the easy one. A fix without a ratchet is a fix with a half-life.

Part three is the boldest and most durable move, and it is not speculative: `async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` is that exact shape, already in the tree, already having caught its class once. The wave's job is to finish what was left at sample scope - and to make the seam list DERIVED rather than hand-maintained, so it cannot silently go stale again.

The slices I lean toward (Decide finalises)

S1 - TOTP, the population of 25. Build a shared window-stable helper: compute the seconds remaining in the current period and, if the headroom is below a threshold, wait out the boundary BEFORE generating, so generation and server validation are guaranteed to land in the same period. Then migrate all 25 sites. Then a tripwire: raw `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` in `api/test/` fails CI. Server code is NOT touched - that is a fence, not a preference.

S2 - OAuth, the seam class. Fix `oauth_test.exs` by isolation-by-construction (the guard's own prescribed remedy: test the predicate by naming/passing config directly rather than globally swapping), OR mark that module `async: false` if the read surface genuinely requires the global. Then GENERALISE the guard: derive the shared-key set instead of hand-listing it, so any config key read by two or more async modules is protected automatically.

S3 - pr-task-gate, the invariant. Re-specify the predicate around what the gate actually means - 'this change is task-backed' - not 'someone is actively typing'. A task closed on met acceptance criteria is the SUCCESS case, not a violation; a well-authored task whose criteria are 'committed / mutation-proven / live run returns X' is legitimately closed before its PR merges, and that deadlocked three PRs today. Two mechanical sub-defects ride along: the workflow has no `types:` filter so it inherits [opened, synchronize, reopened] - adding `edited` lets a corrected PR body re-fire and dissolves the sticky-404. Note the 404 path must STAY definitive: it correctly caught an invented task id today. `scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh` already exists and is the mutation-proof vehicle.

S4 - format. This is a DECIDE-TIME CALL, and it should be argued rather than defaulted. The honest options are (a) fix the 91 files in a session pinned to prod Elixir 1.18.1, or (b) DELETE the job. What is NOT an option is leaving a permanently-red advisory check on screen. The lean is (b)-or-defer: formatting 91 files WILL conflict with two live cycles holding `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` and `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*`, and a deferral stated out loud with its reason is itself a truth-telling act. Silently leaving it is the only losing move.

Direction debate - the rivals, and why this won

RIVAL A - 'Fix the four.' Straight roster execution: four slices, four fixes, four mutation proofs. Bounded, safe, obviously in scope. It loses on the wish's own terms: the wish is not 'these four checks are broken', it is 'gates teach readers to dismiss them'. Four patches with no ratchet leaves the generating process untouched, and the tree already shows what that costs - the seam guard is a wave-old fix whose class immediately regrew in an unlisted key. Rival A would have fixed 1 of 25 TOTP sites and called it done.

RIVAL B - 'Flake observability first.' Build a harness (seed-randomised N-run loop, per-test failure history, a quarantine ledger) before fixing anything, on the theory that you cannot trust gates you cannot measure. Genuinely tempting and it foreclosed the least. It loses on sequencing: the roster is ALREADY proven by hand, by re-run, with the prediction registered before the re-run. Instrumentation would spend the wave and land zero honest gates. Partially absorbed instead: method law already demands 20-30 seed-randomised runs per fix, so that loop gets written as a reusable script rather than a bespoke epic.

RIVAL C - 'Charter first.' This is a founding wave with no charter; make the law the deliverable and the four fixes its proof cases. It loses as a PRIMARY framing - a charter written before the four fixes are attempted would be legislating from theory, and this lead's theory has been corrected twelve times today. Absorbed as a BYPRODUCT: Decide writes D1+ from what the builders actually learn, which is the right order.

WHY THE WINNER WON: it is the only candidate whose success condition is 'the defect class cannot recur', which is the only thing that stops teaching dismissal. And crucially it is not a theory - the repo contains a working instance of the exact shape (the seam guard) AND a working instance of its decay (that guard's one-key list). The evidence for the direction was already in the tree.

The sharpest attack on the winner

SCOPE EXPLOSION. Four gates, a 25-site migration, a derived-seam-key generaliser, a re-specified merge gate with hermetic tests, plus 91 files of formatting - against a hard surface fence and two live cycles in `api/`. This is the attack to take most seriously, and it is how the wave absorbs it:

- The 25-site TOTP migration is MECHANICAL once the helper exists, and `api/test/` is inside our fence, so it collides with nobody. It is one slice, not twenty-five. - The format gate defaults to DEFER-WITH-A-STATED-REASON precisely to remove the 91-file conflict; the wave is allowed to not do it, but not allowed to be quiet about it. - The 'sweep for other contaminated predicates' is SURVEY AND VERIFY work, not build work. It produces filed tasks for wave 2, not slices in wave 1. Width is cheap in the fleets and expensive in the builders.

SECOND ATTACK: the OAuth mechanism is a strategist's reading, not a proof. If the `put_env` collision is not the cause, S2 has no fix. Absorbed by aiming a verifier at exactly one job - reproduce it deterministically (force the interleave, seed 792404, `async: true` audit of `cloud/test/`) BEFORE any builder flies. If reproduction fails, S2 becomes 'instrument and quarantine with a stated reason', which is still honest, and still not a retry wrapper.

THIRD ATTACK: a builder takes the cheap road on S1 and adds drift tolerance to `accounts.ex`, turning a test flake into an auth weakening. Absorbed by making 'server code is not touched' an explicit slice fence, and by pointing the verify fleet at the `totp_opts`/`since:` replay-guard asymmetry before Decide writes the brief.

Method law for this wave (non-negotiable)

A RETRY WRAPPER IS NOT A FIX. It hides the race and preserves the lie. Any slice whose proof is 'it passed this time' is rejected at Review.

EVERY FIX MUST BE PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL. Force the failure condition; show the OLD path breaks there and the NEW one does not. For TOTP that means forcing a window boundary. For OAuth it means forcing the config interleave. Then run the target suite 20-30 times with randomised seeds - not once.

RUN WHERE DEPS RESOLVE. A fresh worktree without `mix deps.get` fails with 'Unknown dependency :ecto_sql given to :import_deps', and at the exit-code level that error is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real failure. A mutation test run there measures the dep error, not the thing. The lead hit this today.

SURFACE FENCE. This cycle owns `api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/`, `cloud/test/`, `.github/workflows/pr-task-gate.yml`, `scripts/pr-task-gate.sh`. S1's population extends the api/test fence to the 8 files holding the 25 call sites. DO NOT touch `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` (Studio wave 11 RUNNING), `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*` (PDS wave 10 RUNNING), `tooling/grip/`, or `api/lib/barkpark/content|portable_doc`.

Survey plan - what the fleet is being sent to find, and why

Fifteen broad assignments, one Sonnet each. Width is cheap here and buys precise depth later. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question, including the ones already believed answered - a strategist's reading is a hypothesis, not a finding.

s1-totp-population - Enumerate all 25 `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` call sites in api/test/ and classify each by the GAP between generation and validation: same-process direct function call, HTTP round-trip, or multi-step. Which are actually boundary-crossable? WHY: Decides whether one helper covers all 25 or the population splits into two shapes needing different remedies.

s2-totp-server-asymmetry - Map every NimbleTOTP.valid? call site in api/lib/. Why does enable_totp/3 pass no opts while valid_totp?/2 and the verify path pass totp_opts(user)? What does `since:` actually guard, and what breaks if they are unified? WHY: The number-one way a builder turns this test fix into a security regression. Must be fenced explicitly in the brief.

s3-oauth-interleave - Confirm or refute: does oauth_test.exs's Application.put_env of the OAuth key (nulling github client_secret) disable github process-wide while router_oauth_test.exs concurrently calls the github callback? Trace how a disabled provider surfaces - is /#oauth_error=oauth_failed the exact symptom? WHY: This is the central OAuth claim and S2's entire basis. If false, S2 needs a different mechanism.

s4-seam-guard-anatomy - Read async_global_seam_guard_test.exs fully. How does it detect offenders, why is @shared_seam_keys hand-maintained, and what would a DERIVED version need - can 'config keys read by 2+ async modules' be computed statically from the test tree? WHY: Determines whether the ratchet for S2 is a one-line list addition or a real generaliser. Feasibility gates ambition.

s5-async-putenv-census - Census every Application.put_env in cloud/test/ AND api/test/: which module, is it async:true, which config key, is it restored on_exit, and is that key read by any other async module? WHY: Sizes the true population behind S2. The seam guard's own moduledoc predicts this list has grown; measure it.

s6-pr-task-gate-invariant - Read scripts/pr-task-gate.sh + pr-task-gate.yml + pr-task-gate.test.sh + docs/ops/merge-gates.md. What invariant do the docs CLAIM, versus what the predicate enforces? Enumerate every state a legitimately-worked task can be in when its PR opens. WHY: S3 rewrites the predicate; it must be rewritten against the real intent, and the doc may already state it correctly.

s7-gate-trigger-mechanics - Confirm pr-task-gate.yml has no `types:` filter (inheriting opened/synchronize/reopened), and establish whether adding `edited` re-fires on a PR body edit. Also check the merge-base grandfather clause and the hotfix! lane for interactions. WHY: The cheapest high-value fix in the wave, and the grandfather/hotfix paths must not be broken by it.

s8-format-gate-truth - Verify the format gate's real state: is it continue-on-error, is it red on main right now, and is the count 91 files (25 lib/, 66 test/)? Is the Elixir 1.18.1-vs-1.19.x formatter-divergence rationale still accurate? WHY: The lead's item 4 was already corrected once from a truncated read. S4's decision needs the real number and the real cause.

s9-format-conflict-map - If the 91 files were formatted, which overlap the two live cycles (api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/, api/tenancy, scripts/pds-*)? Is there a conflict-free subset, and how large? WHY: Decides whether S4 can be scoped safely or must be deferred outright. Determines fix-vs-delete-vs-defer.

Method facts the builders MUST carry (each proven by a live run, not read)

THE DEPS TRAP, reproduced live in two throwaway worktrees. api/.formatter.exs:2 and cloud/.formatter.exs:2 both declare import_deps, which mix format resolves from deps/ ON DISK and never auto-fetches. A git worktree shares no deps/ (gitignored, per-worktree). Fresh worktree, `cd api && mix format --check-formatted` → exit 1, '** (Mix) Unknown dependency :ecto_sql given to :import_deps'; in cloud/ the same run names :ecto instead — the fingerprint is the literal text, not the atom. `mix test` fails differently: 'Unchecked dependencies for environment test' … 'Can't continue due to errors on dependencies'. THE LOAD-BEARING FACT: exit code is 1 in ALL FOUR cases — dep-missing format, genuine format drift, dep-missing test, genuine test failure. Exit code can NEVER discriminate. Only the STDOUT TEXT can. Any builder or mutation harness that checks $? alone will certify a dep-resolution failure as a verdict on the real work. Precondition every brief must carry: run `ls deps` in the target dir first; `mix deps.get` (~4s warm) is sufficient for mix format (no deps.compile needed), and mix test auto-compiles ~76 deps + 800 app files transparently but SLOWLY (>1 min cold) — a tight timeout killing that compile is a third variant of the same contaminated signal. api/ and cloud/ are separate mix projects with separate deps/ and mix.lock; fetching one does not fetch the other. No Makefile target exists for a dev/test deps.get in either.

THE REPRO LOOP needs TWO shapes, and my 'max_cases: 8' was a CI-runner default I repeated without checking. grep across both apps' config/ and mix.exs returns ZERO max_cases settings — both silently inherit Mix's documented default of twice the core count. That is 8 on a 4-vCPU CI runner and 20 on a 10-core dev Mac, a 2.5x concurrency difference that changes the OAuth race window. Any repro must pin `--max-cases 8` explicitly or its result does not transfer. Shape 1 (TOTP, api/): the hazard is real wall clock, so `mix test <file> --repeat-until-failure 30 --max-failures 1` inside one VM is cheap and sufficient. Shape 2 (OAuth, cloud/): NOT that. gr-p5-cloud-flake already PROVED --seed is unreliable for this concurrency class (the same seed gave 1 failure then 0 failures on consecutive runs) and that MODULE-PAIR NARROWING is the technique that reproduces. Worse, `mix help test` warns in its own docs that --repeat-until-failure runs inside one VM and 'if there is any leftover global state after running the tests, re-running the suite may trigger unrelated failures' — a near-exact description of the diagnosed Application.put_env defect, so that flag would CONFOUND the very proof it is being used for. Shape 2 must be an external shell loop booting a fresh VM per iteration over the colliding module pair. CC=/usr/bin/clang is mandatory (the shell's `cc` is a Claude wrapper, not the compiler). No such loop script exists anywhere in scripts/ (69 files checked); it gets built ONCE as a shared artifact, not per-slice.

The S3 builder identified this trap and wrote "I did not file this, and probably should have" - EXPECTED_WORKER now compares against closed_by for done tasks, which is zero-impact today because .github/pr-task-workers.json does not exist, but becomes a false red on a builder-authored PR against a lead-closed task the day anyone adds that map.

What the next wave should take

Branch protection (wave-2 item 1), first and above the rest of the roster. Charter D13 is the load-bearing gap: nothing in this repo is required-by-name, so every ratchet this wave built - all four of them, plus the ones already here - is advisory. This wave made the gates honest; protection is what makes honesty consequential. The path-filter skip-shim is its mandatory first step, because only 2 of 34 workflows run unconditionally on every PR and a required paths-filtered check sits Pending forever and deadlocks the repo. Then, in order: the Quiz.Bridge sandbox cascade (a third distinct hazard shape neither existing fix covers, and it masked 1310 failures in one run); the :barkpark_rate_limiter whole-node ETS seam (which S1's builder hit directly - it is why --repeat-until-failure dies at repetition 3 with HTTP 429); Sobelow's red-under-green; then format completion and promotion once PRs #5016/#5015/#5014 release the Studio bucket. hg-bl-totp-ratchet-cloud-test-root deserves a note: cloud/test has 16 raw TOTP generator sites the api-scoped ratchet structurally cannot see - the exact mirror of charter D6, rediscovered independently one more time.

A gate must red for exactly one reason - its own claim

Living wave Paper for the FOUNDING wave of `auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky` (priority 0). No charter exists yet; this wave's Decide phase writes D1+. Every later phase appends here - Digest adds the survey digest and verify plan, Decide adds the wave plan, Review closes it as the debrief.

STATUS: Strategize complete - the wave is SURVEYING. The direction below is COMMITTED but tentative in its details; two exploration rounds (survey, then verify) precede Decide, which finalises it. Nothing here is a proven claim unless it names the command that produced it.

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard, carried from the wish): Fable 5 is spend-limited. Every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice - never 'fable'.

The wish, verbatim

THIS CYCLE: THE GATES TELL THE TRUTH. Every defect in this roster is a gate that lies - it reds when nothing is wrong, or it blocks work that is correct, and each one teaches readers to dismiss it. A dismissed gate is how a one-character CSS defect survived FIVE waves in production while three gates certified it green. Root task: auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky (priority 0).

What I read, and what it changed

The lead's roster is four proven defects. I read the actual surfaces before setting direction, because a direction set on an unread codebase is a guess - and this lead's briefs have been corrected twelve times today. Four things I found materially reframe the wave. Each is stated with the command that produced it, and each is handed to the verify fleet rather than assumed.

Finding 1 - the TOTP race is real, and the fix must not touch the server

`grep -rn 'NimbleTOTP.verification_code' api/test/` returns 25 call sites across 8 files (accounts_test.exs alone holds 11). The mechanism is confirmed by reading the call site: in `auth_controller_test.exs` `enroll_totp!/1`, the code is computed INLINE while building the request body, then an HTTP round-trip happens. If the 30-second period rolls in that gap, the server correctly rejects a stale code.

CRITICAL GUARDRAIL I want stated before any builder flies: `accounts.ex` `enable_totp/3` is a bare `NimbleTOTP.valid?(secret, code)` with NO drift tolerance, while `valid_totp?/2` and the verify path pass `totp_opts(user)` - which carries `since:`, the REPLAY guard (MEDIUM-6). Those two call sites differ for a reason. A builder who 'unifies' them, or who adds a drift window to make the test pass, converts a test flake into a SECURITY REGRESSION - a gate lying in the other direction, accepting what it should reject. The server is behaving correctly. The fix is entirely test-side.

Finding 2 - the OAuth flake has a named mechanism, and it is not the one filed

The lead's hypothesis was 'shared OAuth state mutated by a concurrent test'. Directionally right, wrong object. I chased and DISCARDED two candidates first: `OAuthStub` stores overrides in the PROCESS DICTIONARY (explicitly async-safe by design), and the `oauth_states` single-use nonce ledger is Repo-backed (sandboxed per async test). Neither can leak.

What can: `cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/oauth_test.exs` is `use BarkparkCloud.DataCase, async: true` and at its 'a provider with blank creds is excluded' test does `Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, patched)` where `patched` nulls github's `client_secret`, asserts `enabled_providers() == ["google"]`, and restores on_exit. `Application.put_env/3` writes ONE value for the WHOLE NODE. While that test holds the swap, github is DISABLED process-wide - and `router_oauth_test.exs`, a different `async: true` module, is calling `/v1/auth/oauth/github/callback`. A disabled provider yields exactly the observed symptom: the FIRST redemption returning `/#oauth_error=oauth_failed` where `#oauth=` was asserted. Seed-dependent, because it is a race.

Finding 3 - the repo already has a tripwire for this exact class, scoped to one key

`cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` exists. It was built for this flake class after `sites_deploy_test.exs` swapped `:site_box_relay` globally and red `router_sites_test.exs`. Its `@shared_seam_keys` list contains exactly ONE entry: `:site_box_relay`. Its own moduledoc closes with a prediction:

Other config keys are swapped by async modules too, but each of those is read by only its own module today; if that ever changes, add the key to @shared_seam_keys rather than re-learning this the hard way.

We are re-learning it the hard way. The `OAuth` config key IS now read by a second async module. The guard's stated precondition is false, and the guard did not notice because the list is hand-maintained. This is the single most important artifact in the wave - it is proof that the fix shape proposed below WORKS, and proof of exactly how it decays when scoped to the one instance that bit us.

Finding 4 - the format gate is not red-by-accident, it is red BY DESIGN

The lead filed this as 'red on main across 91 files'. The file tells a different and worse story. `.github/workflows/elixir.yml` sets the format job `continue-on-error: true`, names it 'Format (mix format --check-formatted, advisory)', and documents WHY: prod pins Elixir 1.18.1, local dev runs 1.19.x, their formatters disagree, and running `mix format` locally is FORBIDDEN by CLAUDE.md. The comment ends: 'until then this job stays visible as a drift signal, not a blocker.'

So this is not a gate that broke. This is a gate that was DECLAWED instead of fixed, and left on screen. It is structurally incapable of being green, it reds every PR including docs-only ones, and it blocks nothing. That is the terminal stage of the disease the wish names - and it is the same story as the one-character CSS defect that survived five waves: a signal nobody could act on, so nobody read it.

The pattern under all four

Each defect is a CORRECT INSIGHT APPLIED AT SAMPLE SCOPE INSTEAD OF POPULATION SCOPE. Nobody here was wrong. Everybody stopped at the instance that bit them.

TOTP - the race is understood; 1 of 25 call sites was going to be fixed. OAuth - the async-global-seam class is understood AND tripwired; the tripwire lists 1 of N keys. pr-task-gate - the invariant is understood ('this change is task-backed'); the predicate encodes one sample of it ('someone is actively typing right now'). format - the toolchain drift is understood; the response was to declaw the signal rather than fix the population of 91 files.

Restated as the law this wave proposes: A GATE MUST BE ABLE TO BE GREEN, ABLE TO BE RED, AND MUST RED FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON - the thing it claims to measure. Every defect here is a predicate contaminated by a variable with nothing to do with its claim: wall clock, scheduler seed, worker liveness, toolchain version. `continue-on-error` is not a third option; it is how a contaminated gate becomes permanent furniture.

DIRECTION - fix populations, and make the hazard unwritable

This wave does NOT fix four failing things. It closes four populations, and leaves each one unable to reopen. Every slice lands in three parts, and a slice missing part three is not done:

(1) THE CAUSE - remove the contaminating variable, never retry around it. (2) THE POPULATION - migrate every sibling instance, not the sample that failed. (3) THE RATCHET - a tripwire that fails CI if the hazardous shape reappears, plus an affordance that makes the safe path the easy one. A fix without a ratchet is a fix with a half-life.

Part three is the boldest and most durable move, and it is not speculative: `async_global_seam_guard_test.exs` is that exact shape, already in the tree, already having caught its class once. The wave's job is to finish what was left at sample scope - and to make the seam list DERIVED rather than hand-maintained, so it cannot silently go stale again.

The slices I lean toward (Decide finalises)

S1 - TOTP, the population of 25. Build a shared window-stable helper: compute the seconds remaining in the current period and, if the headroom is below a threshold, wait out the boundary BEFORE generating, so generation and server validation are guaranteed to land in the same period. Then migrate all 25 sites. Then a tripwire: raw `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` in `api/test/` fails CI. Server code is NOT touched - that is a fence, not a preference.

S2 - OAuth, the seam class. Fix `oauth_test.exs` by isolation-by-construction (the guard's own prescribed remedy: test the predicate by naming/passing config directly rather than globally swapping), OR mark that module `async: false` if the read surface genuinely requires the global. Then GENERALISE the guard: derive the shared-key set instead of hand-listing it, so any config key read by two or more async modules is protected automatically.

S3 - pr-task-gate, the invariant. Re-specify the predicate around what the gate actually means - 'this change is task-backed' - not 'someone is actively typing'. A task closed on met acceptance criteria is the SUCCESS case, not a violation; a well-authored task whose criteria are 'committed / mutation-proven / live run returns X' is legitimately closed before its PR merges, and that deadlocked three PRs today. Two mechanical sub-defects ride along: the workflow has no `types:` filter so it inherits [opened, synchronize, reopened] - adding `edited` lets a corrected PR body re-fire and dissolves the sticky-404. Note the 404 path must STAY definitive: it correctly caught an invented task id today. `scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh` already exists and is the mutation-proof vehicle.

S4 - format. This is a DECIDE-TIME CALL, and it should be argued rather than defaulted. The honest options are (a) fix the 91 files in a session pinned to prod Elixir 1.18.1, or (b) DELETE the job. What is NOT an option is leaving a permanently-red advisory check on screen. The lean is (b)-or-defer: formatting 91 files WILL conflict with two live cycles holding `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` and `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*`, and a deferral stated out loud with its reason is itself a truth-telling act. Silently leaving it is the only losing move.

Direction debate - the rivals, and why this won

RIVAL A - 'Fix the four.' Straight roster execution: four slices, four fixes, four mutation proofs. Bounded, safe, obviously in scope. It loses on the wish's own terms: the wish is not 'these four checks are broken', it is 'gates teach readers to dismiss them'. Four patches with no ratchet leaves the generating process untouched, and the tree already shows what that costs - the seam guard is a wave-old fix whose class immediately regrew in an unlisted key. Rival A would have fixed 1 of 25 TOTP sites and called it done.

RIVAL B - 'Flake observability first.' Build a harness (seed-randomised N-run loop, per-test failure history, a quarantine ledger) before fixing anything, on the theory that you cannot trust gates you cannot measure. Genuinely tempting and it foreclosed the least. It loses on sequencing: the roster is ALREADY proven by hand, by re-run, with the prediction registered before the re-run. Instrumentation would spend the wave and land zero honest gates. Partially absorbed instead: method law already demands 20-30 seed-randomised runs per fix, so that loop gets written as a reusable script rather than a bespoke epic.

RIVAL C - 'Charter first.' This is a founding wave with no charter; make the law the deliverable and the four fixes its proof cases. It loses as a PRIMARY framing - a charter written before the four fixes are attempted would be legislating from theory, and this lead's theory has been corrected twelve times today. Absorbed as a BYPRODUCT: Decide writes D1+ from what the builders actually learn, which is the right order.

WHY THE WINNER WON: it is the only candidate whose success condition is 'the defect class cannot recur', which is the only thing that stops teaching dismissal. And crucially it is not a theory - the repo contains a working instance of the exact shape (the seam guard) AND a working instance of its decay (that guard's one-key list). The evidence for the direction was already in the tree.

The sharpest attack on the winner

SCOPE EXPLOSION. Four gates, a 25-site migration, a derived-seam-key generaliser, a re-specified merge gate with hermetic tests, plus 91 files of formatting - against a hard surface fence and two live cycles in `api/`. This is the attack to take most seriously, and it is how the wave absorbs it:

- The 25-site TOTP migration is MECHANICAL once the helper exists, and `api/test/` is inside our fence, so it collides with nobody. It is one slice, not twenty-five. - The format gate defaults to DEFER-WITH-A-STATED-REASON precisely to remove the 91-file conflict; the wave is allowed to not do it, but not allowed to be quiet about it. - The 'sweep for other contaminated predicates' is SURVEY AND VERIFY work, not build work. It produces filed tasks for wave 2, not slices in wave 1. Width is cheap in the fleets and expensive in the builders.

SECOND ATTACK: the OAuth mechanism is a strategist's reading, not a proof. If the `put_env` collision is not the cause, S2 has no fix. Absorbed by aiming a verifier at exactly one job - reproduce it deterministically (force the interleave, seed 792404, `async: true` audit of `cloud/test/`) BEFORE any builder flies. If reproduction fails, S2 becomes 'instrument and quarantine with a stated reason', which is still honest, and still not a retry wrapper.

THIRD ATTACK: a builder takes the cheap road on S1 and adds drift tolerance to `accounts.ex`, turning a test flake into an auth weakening. Absorbed by making 'server code is not touched' an explicit slice fence, and by pointing the verify fleet at the `totp_opts`/`since:` replay-guard asymmetry before Decide writes the brief.

Method law for this wave (non-negotiable)

A RETRY WRAPPER IS NOT A FIX. It hides the race and preserves the lie. Any slice whose proof is 'it passed this time' is rejected at Review.

EVERY FIX MUST BE PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL. Force the failure condition; show the OLD path breaks there and the NEW one does not. For TOTP that means forcing a window boundary. For OAuth it means forcing the config interleave. Then run the target suite 20-30 times with randomised seeds - not once.

RUN WHERE DEPS RESOLVE. A fresh worktree without `mix deps.get` fails with 'Unknown dependency :ecto_sql given to :import_deps', and at the exit-code level that error is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real failure. A mutation test run there measures the dep error, not the thing. The lead hit this today.

SURFACE FENCE. This cycle owns `api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/`, `cloud/test/`, `.github/workflows/pr-task-gate.yml`, `scripts/pr-task-gate.sh`. S1's population extends the api/test fence to the 8 files holding the 25 call sites. DO NOT touch `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/` (Studio wave 11 RUNNING), `api/tenancy` + `scripts/pds-*` (PDS wave 10 RUNNING), `tooling/grip/`, or `api/lib/barkpark/content|portable_doc`.

Survey plan - what the fleet is being sent to find, and why

Fifteen broad assignments, one Sonnet each. Width is cheap here and buys precise depth later. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question, including the ones already believed answered - a strategist's reading is a hypothesis, not a finding.

s1-totp-population - Enumerate all 25 `NimbleTOTP.verification_code` call sites in api/test/ and classify each by the GAP between generation and validation: same-process direct function call, HTTP round-trip, or multi-step. Which are actually boundary-crossable? WHY: Decides whether one helper covers all 25 or the population splits into two shapes needing different remedies.

What does `since:` actually guard, and what breaks if they are unified? WHY: The number-one way a builder turns this test fix into a security regression. Must be fenced explicitly in the brief.

Trace how a disabled provider surfaces - is /#oauth_error=oauth_failed the exact symptom? WHY: This is the central OAuth claim and S2's entire basis. If false, S2 needs a different mechanism.

s4-seam-guard-anatomy - Read async_global_seam_guard_test.exs fully. How does it detect offenders, why is @shared_seam_keys hand-maintained, and what would a DERIVED version need - can 'config keys read by 2+ async modules' be computed statically from the test tree? WHY: Determines whether the ratchet for S2 is a one-line list addition or a real generaliser. Feasibility gates ambition.

WHY: Sizes the true population behind S2. The seam guard's own moduledoc predicts this list has grown; measure it.

Enumerate every state a legitimately-worked task can be in when its PR opens.
