DIGEST — 15 survey reports folded in; the verify fleet is flying

STATUS: Survey complete. The wave is VERIFYING. 15 surveyors returned; this section states what they established, where they CONTRADICT each other or my direction, what nobody checked, and the 12 verify assignments now in flight. Decide follows the verify round and finalises the slice plan.

What the survey ESTABLISHED

S1 TOTP — settled, and sharper than filed. 25 call sites across 8 files, reproduced independently by three surveyors (grep -rn NimbleTOTP.verification_code api/test/ | wc -l = 25; -rl | wc -l = 8). They split into two shapes, and the split matters for RISK, not for the remedy: 16 are same-process direct calls into Accounts.enable_totp/valid_totp?/verify_totp with zero intervening I/O (microsecond gap, no failure of this shape ever observed), and 9 are HTTP round-trips through Phoenix.ConnTest post() where the gap is tens-to-hundreds of ms. BOTH confirmed real-world failures (auth_controller_test.exs:31 via enroll_totp!/1 driving the :427 failure that red main, and the PR #4920 sighting near :191) are the HTTP shape. One window-stable helper covers both shapes; the migration is uniform mechanical substitution at all 25 sites.

The HARD FENCE is now better-argued than when I wrote it. accounts.ex:598 enable_totp/3 is a bare NimbleTOTP.valid?(secret, code); :632 valid_totp?/2 and :652 verify_totp/2 both pass totp_opts(user) = [since: last_totp_at] (:686). The `since:` guard is NimbleTOTP's reused?/3 (api/deps/nimble_totp/lib/nimble_totp.ex:249-256): it rejects any code whose period floor-divides to <= the since timestamp's period, regardless of digit correctness — the RFC 6238 one-time-use guarantee. enable_totp OMITS it correctly: disable_totp/1 (accounts.ex:617-622) does NOT clear last_totp_at (only reset_mfa:true password reset does, :541-553), so a disable-then-re-enable cycle carries a stale timestamp from the OLD secret into the NEW secret's enrolment — passing totp_opts there would spuriously REJECT a perfectly valid brand-new code. And the trap is baked into the dependency: NimbleTOTP's own moduledoc (deps/nimble_totp/lib/nimble_totp.ex:218-232) PRESCRIBES the grace-window pattern (call valid? at time and at time - period) that a builder chasing this flake would reach for. Doing that on valid_totp?/verify_totp triples the live acceptance window from 30s to ~90s on two internet-facing endpoints (session_controller.ex:372, auth_controller.ex:122) and widens the replay surface MEDIUM-6 exists to close. grep for period:/grace/drift in accounts.ex returns NOTHING today — the fence protects a currently-clean invariant.

S2 OAuth — my strategist's reading was RIGHT, and it is already filed with a reproduction. Four surveyors independently confirmed the mechanism by direct code read: cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/oauth_test.exs:8 is `use DataCase, async: true` and its blank-creds test (:33-44) does Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, patched) at :39, nulling github's client_secret for the whole test body (on_exit restore at :40) — a whole-node write. cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/oauth.ex:329 reads `defp config, do: Application.get_env(...)` FRESH on every call, no caching. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_oauth_test.exs:7 is ALSO async:true and drives GET /v1/auth/oauth/github/callback in ~10 tests. router.ex:898-920 fails at the FIRST `with` clause (OAuth.enabled?) and redirects to /#oauth_error=oauth_failed — never a 404 — which is EXACTLY the asserted-vs-observed mismatch. A third independent CI sighting: run 29744055238 job 88357533276, RouterOAuthTest replay-state test failed then passed on rerun of the identical commit.

CRITICAL for Decide: this is ALREADY a filed, root-caused, reproduced, fix-speced OPEN task — `cloud-oauth-replay-test-is-seed-flaky` (priority 1, 0/7 acceptance criteria, unclaimed). It contains a live reproduction (a probe racing a 50ms blank-creds window deterministically observed {:error, :provider_not_enabled}), proof the seam guard is VACUOUSLY GREEN today, proof that adding the module-form key "OAuth" to @shared_seam_keys flips the guard RED and correctly names oauth_test.exs, and a fix under charter D28 (extract the blank-creds test to an async:false oauth_blank_creds_test.exs + add the key) that explicitly REJECTS retry wrappers and config-injection refactors. It is parented to a DIFFERENT wave paper (production-truth-wave-2026-07-20) and risks sitting orphaned across two waves. Decide ADOPTS and re-parents it. It does NOT re-file it.

The ratchet decay is worse than I diagnosed — it happened TWICE, in two directories, independently. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs is a 63-line pure source-TEXT scanner: Path.wildcard("test/**/*_test.exs") relative to cloud/, keep files containing the literal "async: true", then String.contains? on "Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, #{key}" for each key in a HAND-MAINTAINED @shared_seam_keys (:36) holding exactly [":site_box_relay"]. It only inspects WRITES; it never looks at reads; it cannot discover a new shared key; and it structurally cannot see api/test at all. Meanwhile api/test/barkpark/application_env_isolation_test.exs is the residue of an EARLIER, INDEPENDENT sample-scope fix of the identical class (task-435b89bfa992a58a flipped MediaTest, StudioChatTest and Plugins.GithubTest from async:true to async:false) — and it is a single demonstration test, not a scanner. Two teams, two directories, the same hazard, two correct-but-sample-scoped fixes, neither aware of the other, neither of which swept its own tree. That is the wave's thesis proven twice, not asserted once.

The hazard population is now BOUNDED and countable, which is a real narrowing. Application env is the ONLY live global-state channel: ETS, :persistent_term, named GenServers, and shared-path filesystem writes were all checked across both trees' async:true modules and are CLEAN (the one :ets hit, supervision_isolation_test.exs:104, creates an UNNAMED table; the ~40 Registry.register hits are the app's own BarkparkCloud.Registry domain model, not OTP process registry — a discarded false positive). S3 — THE CONTRADICTION IS SETTLED: task-1471170216ac6b54 IS MISDIAGNOSED, NOT RESOLVED. apply_reap/1 writes worker->nil (:256) and lifecycle->"open" (:269) in ONE Repo.update_all (:284); git log -S puts both in the sweeper's first commit dc90f9071 (2026-05-27) with one commit since; ttl_sweeper_test.exs:126-128 asserts the pair, 12/12 green; the live ledger shows 9 in_progress and 0 with a nil worker. schema.ex:147-161 already names the real cause: a hand-flip around the claim/close engine. The pds-w5-charter-amendment paper quotes the real gate log — "is 'open', not 'in_progress'" — the line-91 message, which the reporter paraphrased as the line-92 one. S3 does NOT absorb it; the task has been annotated and recommended for splitting.

S3 — AND THE RERUN VOLUME MEANS SOMETHING NARROWER THAN CLAIMED. Of 19 attempt>1 runs traced over ~23h: 13 were the task genuinely open/unclaimed at PR-open time (workflow discipline), 4 were the hand-flip in_progress+no-worker state, 1 was a 404 race, 1 was the done case. The two 'stayed red' runs were superseded by fresh successful check-runs on the identical SHA after a manual close+reopen, and both PRs merged clean. Honest green rate 24/25 = 96% against 80% measured; the whole gap is the contaminated predicate. S3 closes the gap; it does not claim to remove the retries.

S4 — THE 'FIX 91 OR DELETE' BINARY WAS FALSE, AND DELETING IS THE LOSING MOVE. Live count at Decide time: 92 files, regenerated and cross-checked; the naive relative-path grep false-positives to 97 on diff-body text. Job-level truth: Format is 10/10 FAILURE on main while every one of those runs concluded 'success' — anyone ranking by run conclusions certifies it green. Requiring it today (no paths filter, runs on every PR) would block 100% of merges repo-wide. cloud.yml:60 runs the IDENTICAL command BLOCKING and green on the IDENTICAL pin — the live counter-example to version skew being the whole cause. So: fix then promote, and never promote to force the fix.

S4 — THE CONFLICT MAP IS KIND, AND VERIFIED TWICE. ZERO PDS-tenancy overlap; scripts/pds-* is structurally unreachable because api/.formatter.exs inputs are scoped under api/. Excluding the Studio bucket, content/portable_doc, and the files owned by S1 and S2 this wave leaves exactly 50 files — recomputed at Decide time, not pasted. The Studio exclusion is live, not precautionary: three currently-open PRs (#5016, #5015, #5014) are editing files in that bucket right now. Toolchain caveat stated rather than glossed: the count was produced under local Elixir 1.19.5 against CI's pinned 1.18.1, and the builder must read its own PR's CI Format output rather than trust the local list.

S5 — A FIFTH INSTANCE OF THE THESIS, PREVIOUSLY UNFILED. The 2026-06-10 never-cancel-main fix (commit a547ff75a, after '19 consecutive main runs cancelled, zero completions all day') reached elixir.yml, go-tests.yml, js-tests.yml, security.yml and pr-task-gate.yml. cloud.yml:28 and doc-gates.yml:237 still say a bare 'cancel-in-progress: true' — re-confirmed by grep at Decide time. Same day's lesson, same class, two files missed. And 'cancelled' is a non-pass: promoting either check before this lands would create a new lying gate as a side effect of the fix for lying gates.

What verification REFUTED or corrected

REFUTED — 'Shape A is a microsecond gap and provably safe' (see the measurement above). REFUTED — 'ETS, persistent_term, named GenServers were swept CLEAN in both trees': the RateLimiter table is a live whole-node ETS seam in api/. REFUTED — 'the ratchet can derive its key set via xref': test files are outside compile scope and the edge can never exist. REFUTED — 'task-1471170216ac6b54's TTL-sweeper mechanism'. REFUTED — the audit task's premise that each cloud key has only one reader: false for TWO keys, and already false at filing time for Cloudflare.

CORRECTED — the grace window DOUBLES the acceptance window (30s -> 60s), it does not triple it, and MEDIUM-6 is NOT widened by the careful variant; the fence's surviving load-bearing claim is narrower and sharper: an expired previous-period code becomes acceptable on two internet-facing endpoints and no test can see it. CORRECTED — the cloud swapper census is 8, not 7. CORRECTED — 'max_cases: 8' was a CI-runner default repeated unchecked; zero max_cases is configured anywhere and the local default is 20 on a 10-core box, a 2.5x difference that changes the race window. CORRECTED — the Sheets EnginePerfTest wall-clock gate the digest called 'live, UNFILED' is filed AND fixed on main (spd-b32, PR #4724, commit 0027ed383) and must not be re-filed. CORRECTED — the format population is 92, and lead-truthgrip's claim on the format task had LAPSED (5h21m against a 45-minute TTL), so it was claimable.

COVERAGE, including the not-founds. Checked and closed NEGATIVE: Billing's node-global swap (safe by construction, FailingRegistry delegates on a process-dictionary miss); Vercel (safe by VALUE — its swap always sets the safe default); :platform_admin_emails (safe by IDENTITY — the allowlist is the test's own random email, and the author's comment shows they reasoned about exactly this); GitHub (sole async:true toucher); OAuthStub and the oauth_states nonce ledger (both discarded on inspection). :usage_fanout_budget_ms is safe only because its population is one file and its in-file defence reasons about TIMING rather than scope — the weakest of the five. NOT REACHED: the five non-Billing cloud keys were cleared only by DIRECT grep for co-readers, which is exactly the method that hid OAuth for months; ~26 of 34 workflows were never green-rated, and go-format.yml and architecture.yml returned ZERO main runs, which is itself unexplained; api/test's two swappers were not checked for second readers; the paper-readers rerun was never traced.

Decisions (mirroring the charter, D1-D16)

D1 Cause + population + ratchet, or the slice is not done — the repo contains the proof twice: two independent sample-scope fixes for the same hazard, neither aware of the other, both already decayed. D2 A retry wrapper is never a fix; every fix is proven ABLE TO FAIL. D3 Exit code can never discriminate a dep error from a verdict — measured 1 in all four cases; only stdout text can. D4 TOTP is fixed in the test, never the server, and the fence is enforced by tests because prose demonstrably is not. D5 The seam ratchet derives nothing — it bans the shape, because xref cannot see test files and text cannot see transitive reads. D6 The ratchet runs over BOTH cloud/test and api/test; the directory gap is why the hazard was rediscovered a second time. D7 The pr-task-gate's invariant is 'task-backed', and done passes only with claim.closed_by. D8 The 404 branch stays definitive, always. D9 Fixtures land before any predicate change. D10 The format gate is fixed then promoted — never deleted, never promoted to force the fix. D11 A partially-clean population still gets a ratchet: the drift ceiling makes it shrink-only. D12 'cancelled' is a non-pass. D13 Nothing is required-by-name; protection is wave-2 work whose first step is a path-filter skip-shim, not a settings toggle. D14 Adopt, never re-file. D15 Measure the thing, not a proxy. D16 --repeat-until-failure is the wrong loop for concurrency races; fresh VM per iteration, --max-cases pinned to CI's 8.

The wave plan — 5 slices, all round 1, all builder_model: opus

S1 hg-w1-totp-window-stable-population (p0, large, api/test/) — one window-stable helper, all 25 sites including the 16 Shape-A ones, two protective fence tests (FENCE A: disable->re-enrol must succeed; FENCE B: a previous-period code must be refused by both live paths, boundary-guarded so it is not itself flaky), and a ratchet banning the raw generator. api/lib is UNCHANGED. Gate: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test over the 8 touched files at --max-cases 8, plus 30 fresh-VM iterations with the RateLimiter ETS table cleared, plus mix format --check-formatted on the touched files.

S2 hg-w1-async-seam-ban-and-scanner (p1, large, cloud/test + 2 api/test files) — isolate all 10 swappers by construction, delete @shared_seam_keys, and ship one predicate the source text can actually answer, over both roots, with an annotated escape hatch. Proven able to fail in BOTH textual forms and proven not to over-match on async:false or on the allowlist. Gate: cd cloud && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test.

S3 hg-w1-pr-task-gate-task-backed (p1, medium, scripts/ + pr-task-gate.yml) — fixtures FIRST (done+worker, cancelled+worker, shown to catch the mutation that today passes 9/9), then the task-backed predicate, then types: gains edited. 404 stays definitive; neutral paths untouched. Gate: bash scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh.

S4 hg-w1-format-drift-ceiling (p2, medium, 50 api files + elixir.yml) — migrate the conflict-free 50, install scripts/format-drift-ceiling.sh as a BLOCKING step against a committed baseline so the remainder can only shrink, rename the job to drop 'advisory', and leave continue-on-error in place with the reason stated. Gate: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix format --check-formatted <the migrated list>, plus the ceiling proven able to fail on a deliberate misformat.

S5 hg-w1-never-cancel-main-population (p2, small, cloud.yml + doc-gates.yml) — give the two missed workflows the 2026-06-10 ref guard and grep all seven to prove no bare 'true' remains. The residual pending-run-collapse mechanism is INFERRED, so it is stated in the PR body and deliberately not remedied. Gate: the grep population check plus both workflows completing on the PR.

FILE-TRUTH: the five slices have disjoint file sets by construction — S4's list explicitly subtracts S1's 8 TOTP files and S2's 2 swappers, S4 owns elixir.yml while S5 owns cloud.yml and doc-gates.yml, and S3 is confined to scripts/ plus pr-task-gate.yml. All five are round 1; nothing in this wave depends on another slice's code being on main.

Backlog filed now, so the ledger shows the future

hg-bl-branch-protection-required-checks (p1) — the reframing that outranks the roster: nothing is required-by-name, and only 2 of 34 workflows run unconditionally, so a required paths-filtered check would sit Pending forever and deadlock the repo. Tier 1 is TWO checks, not eight, and the perf bench is excluded on principle even though it is 10/10 green, because a wall-clock threshold on a shared runner cannot red for exactly one reason. hg-bl-quiz-bridge-sandbox-cascade (p1) — a boot-time PubSub singleton doing unallowed shared-connection Ecto reads; masked 1310 failures in one run; a third hazard shape neither existing fix covers. hg-bl-ratelimiter-ets-whole-node-seam (p1). hg-bl-sobelow-red-under-green (p2) — 8/8 FAILURE beneath green runs, in a security gate. hg-bl-format-complete-and-promote (p2). hg-bl-task-close-landed-prs (p2). hg-bl-disable-totp-stale-last-totp-at (p2). hg-bl-elixir-workflow-no-paths-filter (p3). Four pre-existing tasks were ANNOTATED rather than re-filed: cloud-oauth-replay-test-is-seed-flaky and pr-task-gate-contradicts-close-on-criteria are adopted into their slices; task-04054d483ae95bd1's premise and task-1471170216ac6b54's mechanism are refuted in place with the evidence; and spd-b38-studio-suite-intermittent-red was given the named failing test with full ExUnit output that its own acceptance criterion #1 has been waiting for.

CORRECTION (2026-07-20, Review): the S2 population was 9, not 10

The Decide section above ("S2 - THE POPULATION IS 10, NOT 7") states that cloud/test holds 8 async:true Application env swappers, counting registry/cloudflare_credential_test.exs as the one the filed audit missed. The build refuted that. That file's ONLY occurrence of Application.put_env is moduledoc prose at line 12, saying the token is threaded as an argument and "never smuggled through Application.put_env". It is not a swapper and was correctly left alone.

The true population is 9: seven in cloud/test (oauth, github, billing_reconcile_isolation, vercel, cloudflare, web/router, web/usage_route) and two in api/test (media/image_backend/vix, search/intelligence). The Decide-time census was itself a naive text scan that over-matched on prose - this wave's own thesis applied to this wave's own paperwork, caught by the builder and stamped as a deviation. Left as a dated correction rather than a silent rewrite, per the charter's own standard.

DEBRIEF - what the founding wave actually shipped

All five slices built, reviewed, and green. They five-way merge onto origin/main with no conflicts; on the integrated tree the cloud suite is 2150/0, the api gate suites are 0 failures, and all four new ratchets are green together. GRADE: A.

Per slice, as it will merge

S1 hg-w1-totp-window-stable-population -> loop-epic/totp-window-stable-helper-across-all-25--0-r. All 25 raw generator sites migrated, 0 remaining outside the helper; the helper is a targeted boundary wait proven a no-op on 93.3% of the period by an exhaustive 30,000-offset sweep, not a blanket sleep. Gate on final state: 137 tests / 0 failures at --max-cases 8, format clean, api/lib untouched. The reviewer independently re-proved FENCE B by applying the CAREFUL grace-window mutation (since: threaded through both valid? calls): it reds accounts_test.exs:432 and NOTHING ELSE - a precise detector with zero collateral.

S2 hg-w1-async-seam-ban-and-scanner -> loop-epic/ban-application-put-env-inside-async-tru-1-r. Nine swappers isolated with a per-file comment naming the exact key and, where known, the observed race. @shared_seam_keys deleted; the predicate is now the one question source text can answer, run over BOTH roots from absolute paths, with a reason-required escape hatch and anti-vacuity assertions. cloud 2150/0; cloud/lib unchanged.

S3 hg-w1-pr-task-gate-task-backed -> loop-epic/pr-task-gate-close-the-fixture-hole-firs-2-r. The fixtures-first order was respected and PROVEN: the two new fixtures are the only ones that catch deletion of the lifecycle check, which left the old 9-fixture set fully green. Predicate is now task-backed, not who-is-typing; 404 stays definitive; edited added. 9 -> 20 fixtures, shellcheck clean.

S4 hg-w1-format-drift-ceiling -> loop-epic/migrate-the-50-conflict-free-api-format--3-r. Drift 92 -> 42, population regenerated by measurement rather than pasted, and a shrink-only ceiling installed as its own BLOCKING job - deliberately separate, because continue-on-error is a JOB-level setting and putting the ratchet inside the Format job would have made it unable to fail.

S5 hg-w1-never-cancel-main-population -> loop-epic/cancelled-is-a-non-pass-give-cloud-yml-a-4-r. cloud.yml and doc-gates.yml both carry the ref guard; the population grep across all seven concurrency-bearing workflows returns 0 bare trues, and the whole-tree cross-tab found architecture.yml correctly benign (pull_request-only). Ratchet + bundled selftest, live-mutation proven.

What the review fixed in place

Five defects, and the striking thing is that every one is this epic's own disease living inside a gate built to cure it. That is not an indictment of the builders - it is evidence the standard is genuinely hard to meet, and it is why this wave needed a reviewer rather than a rubber stamp.

1. S5's ratchet went SILENT exactly when it could not run. Under set -e the assignment RESULT="$(scan ...)" aborts the script when scan exits 2, so a missing PyYAML produced exit 2 with a COMPLETELY EMPTY log - stdout and stderr both verified empty before the fix. The script cites charter D3 (only stdout text can discriminate a dep error from a real verdict) and then discarded that text. Both call sites now capture the status and re-emit.

2. S5's predicate UNDER-detected. It read only a literal branches: [main] list, so three valid shapes that DO fire on main were classed PR-only and their bare true passed as a harmless NOTE: push: with no branches filter at all, a glob or scalar (ma*n), and branches-ignore that does not name main. Now fnmatch-resolved with branches-ignore inverted; four new fixtures, and branches-ignore: [main] stays correctly safe.

3. S1's ratchet could pass VACUOUSLY. A wrong @test_root makes Path.wildcard return [], the offender list is trivially empty, and the gate passes having measured nothing. S2's sibling guard in this same wave defends exactly this; S1's did not - the two ratchets held different standards for their own honesty. Now asserts >100 files scanned and that the allowlisted helper is among them; proven able to fail.

4. S2's predicate missed formatter-WRAPPED use declarations and put_all_env. mix format splits a long "use ...Case, async: true" across two lines, and the per-line async match saw neither half - a module could carry a node-global put_env straight through the ratchet. Both closed, pinned by four fixtures including a wrapped async: FALSE case so the continuation-joining cannot become an over-matcher.

5. S3 read its parser output WHITESPACE-split. Nothing constrains a ledger claim.worker to a slug, and a value containing a space shifted every later field one position - the gate then returned a confident verdict computed from the wrong values. Worst case was a FALSE PASS: EXPECTED_WORKER=fable matching a task claimed by 'fable tob'. Now tab-separated, with tabs and newlines squashed at the emitter so the separator cannot be forged from the data side.

Two things the lead must know before merging

S4's toolchain skew is smaller than filed but still OPEN. The format-ceiling job is BLOCKING with no paths filter, and the roster was generated on local Elixir 1.19.5 against CI's pinned 1.18.1. New measurement this review: the entire cloud/ tree is format-clean under local 1.19.5, and cloud.yml runs the identical check BLOCKING and GREEN on the pin - a project's worth of Elixir on which the two formatters agree byte-for-byte. That does NOT cover the 50 migrated files' specific constructs. Read the PR's own format-ceiling job output. If it reds on files nobody touched, REGENERATE .format-drift-ceiling on the pin; never add continue-on-error to the ceiling job.

S1 x S4 interaction: settled by running it, not by arguing. S1's builder warned the two slices could disagree by up to 8 files if S4 committed a baseline computed before S1 merged. A real merge of the two branches shows the ceiling PASSES at 39 against its ceiling of 42 and names exactly the three roster files S1 formatted, with the lower-the-baseline notice. Shrink-only does the right thing. After both merge, lower count: to 39 and drop those three lines.

Merge-gated criteria the LEAD closes, one per slice: S1 criterion 9, S2 criterion 8, S3 criterion 7, S4 criterion 8, S5 criterion 4 - all worded "PR merged to main". S5 criterion 2 is additionally unproven at builder scope (it requires the PR's own cloud.yml and doc-gates.yml checks to CONCLUDE with quoted names and conclusions) and is honestly stamped --miss, as is S4's criterion 1 attempt note on toolchain skew. Neither is a stall; both need a real CI run.

Ledger audit

Clean. All five slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with claims held, evidence stamped as the work happened rather than batched, and merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - exactly the contract. Both honest --miss notes (S4 criterion 1, S5 criterion 2) are present with substantive text rather than a bare flag. Every honest-gates task updated today is a child of the epic; nothing outside the wave was touched. Twelve backlog children are filed, published and open.

One ledger addition by the reviewer: hg-bl-pr-task-gate-expected-worker-actor-drift (p3). The S3 builder identified this trap and wrote "I did not file this, and probably should have" - EXPECTED_WORKER now compares against closed_by for done tasks, which is zero-impact today because .github/pr-task-workers.json does not exist, but becomes a false red on a builder-authored PR against a lead-closed task the day anyone adds that map.

What the next wave should take

Branch protection (wave-2 item 1), first and above the rest of the roster. Charter D13 is the load-bearing gap: nothing in this repo is required-by-name, so every ratchet this wave built - all four of them, plus the ones already here - is advisory. This wave made the gates honest; protection is what makes honesty consequential. The path-filter skip-shim is its mandatory first step, because only 2 of 34 workflows run unconditionally on every PR and a required paths-filtered check sits Pending forever and deadlocks the repo. Tier 1 is TWO checks on day one, not eight.

Then, in order: the Quiz.Bridge sandbox cascade (a third distinct hazard shape neither existing fix covers, and it masked 1310 failures in one run); the :barkpark_rate_limiter whole-node ETS seam (which S1's builder hit directly - it is why --repeat-until-failure dies at repetition 3 with HTTP 429); Sobelow's red-under-green; then format completion and promotion once PRs #5016/#5015/#5014 release the Studio bucket. hg-bl-totp-ratchet-cloud-test-root deserves a note: cloud/test has 16 raw TOTP generator sites the api-scoped ratchet structurally cannot see - the exact mirror of charter D6, rediscovered independently one more time.

The direction: fix populations, not samples, and leave a ratchet so each hazard becomes unwritable.
